mainTopic: How the ספר תורה and the שברי לוחות fit in the ארון according to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, then the order of the books of נביאים and כתובים and who wrote them
overview: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה's teaching that the שברי לוחות were also in the ארון. The גמרא then asks a size question. A ספר תורה six טפחים around is two טפחים thick, so how did it fit into the two-טפחים space רבי מאיר leaves for it? רב אחא בר יעקב and רב אשי answer this. The גמרא then fills gaps in each opinion: where the scroll sat for רבי יהודה before the ארגז came, how רבי מאיר reads 'מצד הארון', and where the עמודין stood. It also asks how רבי מאיר knows the שברי לוחות were in the ארון. רב הונא's 'שם שם' is offered first. That answer is set aside because 'שם שם' is needed for רבי יוחנן's teaching, so רבי מאיר learns it from 'אשר שברת ושמתם' instead. The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה uses each of these פסוקים too. A new ברייתא then gives the order of the books of נביאים and כתובים, and the גמרא explains why הושע, ישעיה and איוב are placed where they are. Finally the ברייתא begins listing who wrote each book: משה, יהושע, שמואל, and דוד with ten elders. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: the broken tablets were also in the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the ברייתא teach that the שברי לוחות were placed in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: …the broken pieces of the tablets, which were placed in the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the ברייתא from the previous section. It teaches that the broken first tablets were also kept in the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה reads the extra limiting words of the פסוק 'אין בארון רק' as including more items. One of those items is the שברי לוחות. The גמרא will come back to this point at the end of this section.

keyTerms.meaning: The broken pieces of the first tablets, which משה broke
The Ark in the משכן and the בית המקדש

phrases.english: the broken pieces of the tablets, which are placed in the Ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שברי לוחות were kept inside the ארון together with the whole לוחות.

steps.title: A six-טפחים scroll can't fit in a two-טפחים space
steps.stepSummary: If a ספר תורה is six טפחים around, it is at least two טפחים thick. Rolled from both ends, it is even thicker. So how did it fit into רבי מאיר's two-טפחים space?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think a Torah scroll's circumference is six handbreadths, then here is a problem. Anything with a circumference of three handbreadths is one handbreadth wide. And since the scroll is rolled toward its middle, it is more than two handbreadths, because of the space between the rolls. So how could it sit in a space of only two handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier statement that a ספר תורה is six טפחים around. It shows that such a scroll could not fit into the two-טפחים space that רבי מאיר says was left for it in the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The math rule is simple: something three טפחים around is one טפח across. So a scroll six טפחים around is two טפחים across. A normal ספר תורה is rolled from both ends toward the middle, which makes two rolls with gaps between them. That pushes it past two טפחים, so it cannot fit into exactly two טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Its circumference, the distance around it
Rolled toward its middle, with a roller at each end
Handbreadths (here, the space of two טפחים)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether the ספר תורה was in the ארון. It is only about the size math: a scroll two טפחים thick plus gaps cannot squeeze into exactly two טפחים.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a Torah scroll's circumference is six handbreadths;

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהֶקֵּיפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים –
phrases.english: now, anything that has a circumference of three handbreadths
has a width of one handbreadth,
and since it is rolled toward its middle,
it comes to more than two handbreadths
because of the space in between;
phrases.notes: He means the gap between the two rolls of the scroll.

phrases.english: how does it fit in two handbreadths?
phrases.notes: Two טפחים is the space רבי מאיר's ברייתא leaves for the ספר תורה inside the ארון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הֶקֵּיפוֹ שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא, the גמרא uses רבי מאיר's measurements to challenge the earlier statement about the scroll's size.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that a ספר תורה is six טפחים around
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Six טפחים around means two טפחים across. A scroll rolled from both ends adds gaps, so it is wider than the two-טפחים space רבי מאיר gives it.

steps.title: The courtyard scroll was rolled from one end only
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב: the ספר עזרה in the ארון was rolled onto a single roller, so it had no gap between two rolls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The scroll of the Temple courtyard was rolled to its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the special scroll kept in the ארון was rolled from one end only, as a single roll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in the question was the extra space from two rolls with a gap between them. A single roll removes that gap. That brings the scroll down to two טפחים across.

keyTerms.meaning: The special ספר תורה kept in the Temple courtyard, the one placed in the ארון
Rolled to its beginning, onto one roller

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
The scroll of the courtyard was rolled to its beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב סֵפֶר עֲזָרָה לִתְחִלָּתוֹ הוּא נִגְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the size challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the scroll in the ארון was rolled differently from a regular scroll.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scroll was rolled from both ends, like a regular ספר תורה, so it was more than two טפחים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ספר עזרה was a single roll, so there was no extra gap.

steps.title: Still, two טפחים can't fit in exactly two טפחים
steps.stepSummary: Even as a single roll, the scroll is two טפחים across. How does that fit into a space of exactly two טפחים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, how does something two handbreadths wide sit in two handbreadths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses further. Even with one roll, the scroll exactly fills the space, and an object can't be slid into a space that is exactly its own size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's answer only removed the extra width from the gap. The scroll is still two טפחים across, which leaves no room at all to put it in or take it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Two in two: something two wide in a space two wide

phrases.english: But still, how does two sit in two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's answer as not enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single roll is still exactly two טפחים, so it cannot be placed into a two-טפחים space.

steps.title: A small part was rolled separately and placed on top
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: a small section of the scroll was rolled by itself and laid on top, so the main roll was less than two טפחים across.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: A little of it was rolled separately, and that roll was placed on top.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final answer. A small part of the scroll was rolled on its own and set above the main roll, making the main roll thinner than two טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking some of the parchment off the main roll makes that roll a bit thinner, so it now fits with room to spare. The small extra roll sits higher up, above the main roll, so it does not take up width.
steps.whatToRemember: Size problem: six טפחים around means two טפחים across. רב אחא בר יעקב: a single roll means no gap. רב אשי: a small part was rolled separately and placed on top, so the main roll fits.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A little of it was rolled up, and that roll was placed on top.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי דְּכָרֵיךְ בֵּיהּ פּוּרְתָּא וְכַרְכֵיהּ לְעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the leftover problem from the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a practical detail about how the scroll was arranged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole scroll was one roll exactly two טפחים thick.
steps.terutzMaskana: Part was rolled separately and placed above, so the main roll was under two טפחים.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה: where was the ספר תורה before the ארגז came?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the ספר תורה rested on the ארגז sent by the פלשתים. Where did it rest before that chest arrived?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה: before the chest arrived, where did the Torah scroll sit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the details of the ברייתא and asks a gap question about רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארגז only came in the days of the פלשתים, long after משה placed the ספר תורה by the ארון. So רבי יהודה needs a place for the scroll in all the earlier years.

keyTerms.meaning: The chest the פלשתים sent along with the ארון when they returned it

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda,
before the chest came,
phrases.notes: This is the chest the פלשתים sent back with the ארון in the days of שמואל.

phrases.english: how did the Torah scroll sit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִקַּמֵּי דְּלַיְתֵי אַרְגַּז סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה הֵיכִי הֲוָה יָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size question to clarifying each opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the ספר תורה rested, according to רבי יהודה, before the ארגז existed.

steps.title: A shelf stuck out from the ארון
steps.stepSummary: A board stuck out from the ארון, and the ספר תורה rested on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A shelf stuck out from it, and the Torah scroll sat on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a board stuck out from the side of the ארון, and the ספר תורה sat on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי יהודה's view that the scroll was outside the ארון, beside it. Before the ארגז came, a shelf attached to the ארון held it.

phrases.english: A shelf would stick out from it,
and the Torah scroll sat on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A shelf stuck out from the ארון and held the ספר תורה.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר: what does 'מצד הארון' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to put the ספר תורה 'at the side of the ארון'. How does רבי מאיר, who puts it inside, explain this?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: what does he do with the phrase 'at the side of the Ark'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר with a פסוק that seems to say the ספר תורה was next to the ארון, not inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מצד ארון' sounds like outside, beside the ארון, which is רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר must explain how he reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: At the side of the Ark (דברים 31:26)
What does he do with it? How does he explain it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
this phrase 'at the side of the Ark', what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַאי מִצַּד אֲרוֹן מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יהודה to a gap in רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view that the ספר תורה was inside the ארון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'at the side of the ארון', which sounds like outside.

steps.title: Beside the tablets, not between them, but still inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'מצד' as 'beside the לוחות', not between them. The ספר תורה was inside the ארון, off to the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that phrase to teach that it was placed at the side, and not placed between the tablets. Really it was inside, at the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר reads the word 'מצד' as describing a spot inside the ארון, beside the לוחות and not between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on the words of the פסוק but read 'side' differently. רבי יהודה: the side of the outside of the ארון. רבי מאיר: inside the ארון, at the side of the לוחות.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (to teach something else)

phrases.english: He needs that
to teach that it is placed at the side
and is not placed between the tablets;
but really it was inside it, at the side.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ דְּמִתְּנַח לֵיהּ מִצַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from 'מצד ארון'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the פסוק: 'side' means beside the לוחות inside the ארון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מצד' means outside, next to the ארון.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the scroll was inside the ארון, beside the לוחות and not between them.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר: where did the columns stand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the עמודין stood according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, where did the columns stand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks another detail question about רבי מאיר's layout of the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's measurements use up the space inside the ארון with the לוחות, the walls and the ספר תורה. So it is unclear where the עמודין could fit.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, עַמּוּדִין הֵיכָא הֲווֹ קָיְימִי?
phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, where did the columns stand?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר עַמּוּדִין הֵיכָא הֲווֹ קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues clarifying רבי מאיר's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location of the עמודין in רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: The columns stood outside
steps.stepSummary: The עמודין stood outside the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: the עמודין were outside the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר leaves no spare room inside, the עמודין must have stood outside the ארון. This keeps his measurements intact.

phrases.english: Outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the עמודין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עמודין stood outside the ארון.

steps.title: For רבי מאיר: how does he know the broken tablets were in the ארון?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the שברי לוחות from 'אין בארון רק', but רבי מאיר uses that פסוק for the ספר תורה. So what is רבי מאיר's source?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר: the broken tablets that were placed in the Ark, from where does he know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's source that the שברי לוחות were in the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה learns the שברי לוחות from the extra words of 'אין בארון רק'. רבי מאיר uses those words to place the ספר תורה inside, so he needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? What is his source?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
the broken tablets that are placed in the Ark,
from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר שִׁבְרֵי לוּחוֹת דְּמוּנָּחִין בָּאָרוֹן מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ending of the ברייתא from step 1 and asks how רבי מאיר derives it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי מאיר's source for the שברי לוחות being in the ארון.

steps.title: From רב הונא: the double 'שם שם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns it from רב הונא. The double word 'שם שם' in the פסוק teaches that both the לוחות and the שברי לוחות were in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from רב הונא, as רב הונא said: What is meant by what is written, 'whereupon is called the Name, the Name of the Lord of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim'? This teaches that the tablets and the broken tablets were placed in the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר uses רב הונא's דרשה. The repeated word 'שם' points to two sets of tablets in the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the ארון says 'שם' twice. Each 'שם' points to one set of tablets carrying the Name: the whole second לוחות and the broken first ones. This gives רבי מאיר his source without using 'אין בארון רק'.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, he learns it from
What is meant by what is written?
'Name, Name': the double word the דרשה is built on

steps.whatToRemember: So far: רבי יהודה says the ספר תורה was outside, first on a shelf and later on the ארגז, and he learns the שברי לוחות from 'אין בארון רק'. רבי מאיר says the ספר תורה was inside, beside the לוחות, and the עמודין were outside. For רבי מאיר's source for the שברי לוחות, the גמרא first offers רב הונא's 'שם שם'. Step 15 will challenge this source, and step 17 gives the one that stands.

phrases.english: He derives it from Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said: What is meant by what is written:
'whereupon is called the Name, the Name of
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:2. Notice the word 'שם' appears twice in a row.

phrases.english: the Lord of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim'?
It teaches that the tablets and the broken tablets
are placed in the Ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי מאיר's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא's דרשה on the double 'שם' shows both sets of tablets were in the ארון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how each opinion is built: once רבי מאיר uses one פסוק for the ספר תורה, he needs a separate פסוק for the שברי לוחות.

steps.title: What רבי יהודה learns from 'שם שם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not need 'שם שם' for the שברי לוחות. He uses it for רבי יוחנן's teaching that God's Name and all His other names were placed in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהודה, what does he do with 'שם שם'? He needs it for what רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: it teaches that God's Name and all His other names were placed in the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with the extra word 'שם', and answers that he uses it for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already has a source for the שברי לוחות ('אין בארון רק'), so 'שם שם' seems unused in his view. The גמרא explains that he reads 'שם' as 'name': God's Name and all His names were in the ארון.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
He needs it (for a different teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: 'וְאִידַּךְ' means 'the other one'. Here it points to רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר. The גמרא keeps switching back and forth, so check each time who 'the other one' is.

phrases.english: And the other one, what does he do with this?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is רבי יהודה, who already learned the broken tablets from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: He needs that for the teaching of רבי יוחנן,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: as רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי:
This teaches that the Name of God and all His other names
were placed in the ארון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – הַהוּא מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing רבי מאיר's source ('שם שם'), the גמרא explains how רבי יהודה uses that same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי יהודה learn from 'שם שם'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns רבי יוחנן's teaching that God's Name and all His names were placed in the ארון.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר needs 'שם שם' for that too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי מאיר should also need 'שם שם' for רבי יוחנן's teaching, so he cannot use it for the שברי לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the other one, רבי מאיר, also needs this פסוק for that same teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's source. If 'שם שם' teaches about God's Name, רבי מאיר needs it for that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's teaching is not just רבי יהודה's view. Everyone should agree with it. So the פסוק is already used up, and רבי מאיר seems to have no source left for the שברי לוחות.

phrases.english: But the other one also needs it for this!
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 14's teaching to undo the source given to רבי מאיר in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's use of 'שם שם' (step 13) for the שברי לוחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is needed for רבי יוחנן's teaching, which רבי מאיר also accepts, so it cannot also be his source for the שברי לוחות.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees and asks again for רבי מאיר's source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the objection is correct, so it asks again: where does רבי מאיר learn that the שברי לוחות were in the ארון?
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. So where does רבי מאיר learn that the broken tablets were placed in the ארון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and drops the 'שם שם' answer. It reopens the question of רבי מאיר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אין הכי נמי' is an admission. The answer from רב הונא no longer works for רבי מאיר. The question from step 12 is open again and needs a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (an admission)
The broken pieces of the first tablets
From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so.
But then, that the broken tablets were placed in the ארון,
where does he learn it from?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הָכִי נָמֵי. אֶלָּא שִׁבְרֵי לוּחוֹת דְּמוּנָּחִין בָּאָרוֹן מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with the קשיא of step 15 and reopens the question of step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A new source for רבי מאיר that the שברי לוחות were in the ארון.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns it from רב יוסף's reading of 'אשר שברת ושמתם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns it from a ברייתא of רב יוסף: 'אשר שברת ושמתם' teaches that both the לוחות and the broken pieces were placed in the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from what רב יוסף taught: 'which you broke, and you shall put them'. This teaches that both the tablets and the broken tablets were placed in the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר a new source. It reads the פסוק about the tablets משה broke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the broken tablets ('אשר שברת') and then says 'ושמתם', put them in the ארון. Reading these together teaches that the broken tablets were put in the ארון along with the new ones.

phrases.english: He derives it from what רב יוסף taught,
as רב יוסף taught:
"Which you broke, and you shall put them"
This teaches that the tablets and the broken tablets
were placed in the ארון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reopened question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns it from 'אשר שברת ושמתם' (רב יוסף's ברייתא).

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses 'אשר שברת' for ריש לקיש's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not need 'אשר שברת' for the broken tablets. He uses it for ריש לקיש: God told משה 'יישר כחך' for breaking the tablets.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהודה, what does he do with this פסוק? He needs it for what ריש לקיש said: 'which you broke' means God said to משה, 'Well done for breaking them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יהודה does with רבי מאיר's new source, so that no פסוק goes unused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads 'אשר' as similar to 'יישר'. That turns the words into praise: God approved of משה breaking the tablets. This closes the topic: each opinion has a source, and each פסוק has a use.

keyTerms.meaning: May your strength be straight; well done
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: רבי יהודה learns the שברי לוחות from 'אין בארון רק', and uses 'שם שם' for God's Name and 'אשר שברת' for יישר כחך. רבי מאיר learns the שברי לוחות from 'אשר שברת ושמתם'.

phrases.english: And the other one, what does he do with it?
He needs that for the teaching of ריש לקיש,
as ריש לקיש said:
"Which you broke"
phrases.notes: He hears 'אשר' like 'יישר', which is the source of the praise that follows.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to משה:
Well done, that you broke them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יהודה uses the פסוק that step 17 gave to רבי מאיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי יהודה learn from 'אשר שברת'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש's teaching that God told משה 'יישר כחך ששברת'.

steps.title: The order of the books of נביאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the order of the books of נביאים: יהושע, שופטים, שמואל, מלכים, ירמיה, יחזקאל, ישעיה, and the Twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the order of the Prophets is יהושע and שופטים, שמואל and מלכים, ירמיה and יחזקאל, ישעיה and the Twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that gives the order of the books of נביאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list puts ישעיה after ירמיה and יחזקאל, and puts the Twelve last. That order will be questioned in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Prophets; the books of the Prophets
The Twelve (the book of the twelve shorter prophets, תרי עשר)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The order of the Prophets is:
Joshua and Judges, Samuel and Kings,
Jeremiah and Ezekiel, Isaiah and the Twelve.
phrases.notes: 'The Twelve' is the one book holding the twelve short prophets, and הושע is the first of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the ארון discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The order of נביאים: יהושע, שופטים, שמואל, מלכים, ירמיה, יחזקאל, ישעיה, תרי עשר.

steps.title: הושע came first, so the Twelve should come first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the order. הושע was the first of the four prophets of his time, ahead of ישעיה, so his book (the Twelve) should come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, הושע came earlier. The פסוק says 'God first spoke to הושע'. But was הושע really the first prophet? There were many prophets from משה until הושע! רבי יוחנן explained: he was the first of four prophets who prophesied in that period, הושע, ישעיה, עמוס and מיכה. So הושע should be placed first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's order. It uses a פסוק and רבי יוחנן's explanation to show that הושע was earlier than ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק cannot mean הושע was the first prophet ever. רבי יוחנן explains it means he was first among the four prophets of his era. Since ישעיה came after הושע, the Twelve, which starts with הושע, should be placed before ישעיה, not after him.

keyTerms.meaning: So let it be placed first

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not why הושע's book comes after other books in general. It is why the Twelve, which includes הושע, comes after ישעיה, who prophesied after הושע.

phrases.english: Consider: הושע came earlier,
as it is written: "When God first spoke to הושע".
But did God speak with הושע first?
Weren't there, from משה until הושע,
many prophets!
And רבי יוחנן said:
He was the first of four prophets
who prophesied in that period,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: הוֹשֵׁעַ וִישַׁעְיָה, עָמוֹס וּמִיכָה;
phrases.english: and they are: הושע and ישעיה, עמוס and מיכה.
So let הושע be placed first!
phrases.notes: He means the Twelve, which opens with הושע, should come before ישעיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order given in the ברייתא of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's placing of the Twelve (with הושע) last, after ישעיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Books should follow the order in time. הושע prophesied before ישעיה, so the book that contains הושע should come first.

steps.title: הושע is grouped with the last prophets
steps.stepSummary: Because הושע's prophecy is written in one book together with חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי, who were the last prophets, the whole book is counted with them at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since his prophecy is written together with חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי, and they were the last of the prophets, he is counted with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 about why the Twelve, which opens with הושע, comes last instead of first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The book of the Twelve is one unit. Its placement follows its latest prophets, חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי, not its earliest one. So הושע goes to the end along with them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Twelve, the single book of the twelve shorter prophets
The last three prophets, from the time of the second בית המקדש
He is counted together with them

phrases.english: Since his prophecy is written
together with Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi,
and Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi
were the last of the prophets –
he is counted with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב נְבוּאֲתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי חַגַּי זְכַרְיָה וּמַלְאָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: The book's position follows its latest prophets
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הושע was earliest, so the Twelve should come first
steps.terutzMaskana: The Twelve is one book and goes with its last prophets, at the end

steps.title: Why not write הושע as a separate book?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: then write הושע as his own book and place it first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him be written separately, and let him be placed first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: if the only problem is that הושע is attached to the late prophets, separate him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 21 depended on הושע being bound up with חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי. The challenge asks why that binding is necessary at all. A separate book of הושע could then come first, in its proper time order.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be written on its own

phrases.english: But let it be written separately,
and let it come first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that הושע must be placed with the last prophets
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he could be written separately, he could be placed first by time order

steps.title: A small book would get lost
steps.stepSummary: הושע is too short to stand alone; as a separate scroll it would get lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is small, it would get lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why הושע is not written as a separate book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny scroll could easily go missing. Joining the short prophets into one book protects them. So the Twelve stays together, and its position follows the last prophets.

phrases.english: Since it is small, it would get lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הושע could be its own book and come first
steps.terutzMaskana: A short book alone would be lost, so it stays in the Twelve

steps.title: ישעיה was earlier, so why is he placed later?
steps.stepSummary: ישעיה lived before ירמיה and יחזקאל, so his book should come before theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, ישעיה came before ירמיה and יחזקאל. Let ישעיה be placed first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the order in the ברייתא of step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ירמיה, יחזקאל, then ישעיה. If the order follows time, ישעיה, who was earlier, should come before both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Look now / consider (opens a logical point)

phrases.english: Consider: Isaiah came earlier
than Jeremiah and Ezekiel,
let Isaiah be placed first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the order of נביאים
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing ישעיה after ירמיה and יחזקאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Books should follow time order, and ישעיה was earlier

steps.title: Destruction next to destruction, comfort next to comfort
steps.stepSummary: The order follows content: מלכים ends with חורבן, ירמיה is all חורבן, יחזקאל moves from חורבן to נחמה, and ישעיה is all נחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since מלכים ends with destruction, ירמיה is all destruction, יחזקאל begins with destruction and ends with comfort, and ישעיה is all comfort, we put destruction next to destruction and comfort next to comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the order of these books follows their themes, not the time the prophets lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each book is placed next to the book whose theme matches it. מלכים ends with חורבן, so ירמיה, which is all חורבן, follows. יחזקאל moves from חורבן to נחמה, which leads into ישעיה, which is all נחמה.

keyTerms.meaning: We place next to each other

steps.whatToRemember: The order of נביאים mostly follows time, but ירמיה, יחזקאל, ישעיה are arranged by theme: from destruction to comfort.

phrases.english: Since Kings ends with destruction;
and Jeremiah is all destruction;
and Ezekiel begins with destruction
and ends with comfort;
and Isaiah is all comfort –
we place destruction next to destruction,
and comfort next to comfort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Order by theme rather than by time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ישעיה should come first because he was earlier
steps.terutzMaskana: Books are grouped by theme: חורבן next to חורבן, נחמה next to נחמה

steps.title: The order of כתובים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the order of כתובים: רות, תהלים, איוב, משלי, קהלת, שיר השירים, קינות, דניאל, אסתר, עזרא, דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of כתובים: רות, תהלים, איוב, משלי, קהלת, שיר השירים, קינות, דניאל, מגילת אסתר, עזרא, and דברי הימים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on from נביאים and gives the order of the books of כתובים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next questions. Just as the גמרא questioned the order of נביאים, it will now question parts of this list, starting with איוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Writings, the third section of תנ"ך

phrases.english: The order of the Writings:
Ruth, the book of Psalms, Job, and Proverbs,
Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs, and Lamentations,
Daniel and the Scroll of Esther,
Ezra and Chronicles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from נביאים to כתובים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fixed order of the eleven books of כתובים

steps.title: If איוב lived in משה's time, he should come first
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that איוב lived in the time of משה, his book is the oldest and should open כתובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says איוב lived in the days of משה, let איוב be placed first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of כתובים based on one opinion about when איוב lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If איוב lived in משה's time, he is far earlier than רות or דוד. By time order, his book should come first, not third.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
איוב lived in the days of משה

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
Job lived in the days of Moses,
let Job be placed first!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אִיּוֹב בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order given in step 26
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By time order, the earliest book should come first

steps.title: We don't begin with suffering
steps.stepSummary: כתובים should not open with a book of suffering like איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not begin with suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that איוב is not placed first because its subject is suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if איוב is the oldest, opening כתובים with a book full of suffering is not proper. So the content outweighs the time order here.

phrases.english: We do not begin with suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איוב is oldest, so it should come first
steps.terutzMaskana: A book of suffering should not open כתובים

steps.title: But רות is also about suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רות, which does open כתובים, is also a story of suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ruth is also suffering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 28 using the book that actually comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כתובים may not open with suffering, why does it open with רות? The book of רות also tells of hardship and loss.

phrases.english: Ruth is also suffering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that we do not begin with suffering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רות, which is first, is also about suffering

steps.title: רות's suffering has a happy ending
steps.stepSummary: רות is suffering that leads to a good future: from her came דוד, who filled הקדוש ברוך הוא with songs and praises, as רבי יוחנן says.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is suffering that has a good ending. As רבי יוחנן said: Why was she named רות? Because from her came דוד, who filled הקדוש ברוך הוא with songs and praises.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רות's suffering is different because it ends well, and brings רבי יוחנן's teaching to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not against any suffering at all, only against suffering with no hopeful outcome. רות's story ends with the line of דוד, and her very name hints at this. So it may open כתובים, but איוב may not.

keyTerms.meaning: Who satisfied Him, filled Him (to the full)

steps.whatToRemember: כתובים does not open with suffering, but suffering that leads to a good future, like רות leading to דוד, is fine to open with.

phrases.english: It is suffering that has a good future –
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Why was her name called Ruth?
Because from her came David,
who filled the Holy One, Blessed be He,
phrases.notes: A play on words: רות sounds like ריוה, "to fill up" or "to satisfy".

phrases.english: with songs and praises.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רות is suffering, so it should not come first either
steps.terutzMaskana: Suffering with a good outcome may open כתובים

steps.title: Who wrote the books: משה, יהושע, שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins listing authors: משה wrote the תורה, פרשת בלעם, and איוב; יהושע wrote his book and eight פסוקים in the תורה; שמואל wrote his book, שופטים, and רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who wrote them? משה wrote his book, the section of בלעם, and איוב. יהושע wrote his book and eight פסוקים in the תורה. שמואל wrote his book, שופטים, and רות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new topic: who wrote each book of תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people wrote more than their own book. משה also wrote איוב, יהושע wrote eight פסוקים of the תורה, and שמואל also wrote שופטים and רות.

phrases.english: And who wrote them?
Moses wrote his own book
and the section of Balaam, and Job.
Joshua wrote his own book
and eight verses in the Torah.
Samuel wrote his own book
and Judges, and Ruth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section of the ברייתא, from order of books to their authors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה, יהושע, and שמואל each wrote their own book plus additional sections

steps.title: דוד wrote תהלים using ten elders
steps.stepSummary: דוד wrote ספר תהלים including works of ten earlier elders, such as אדם הראשון, מלכי צדק, אברהם, משה, הימן, ידותון, and אסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד wrote ספר תהלים through ten elders: through אדם הראשון, מלכי צדק, אברהם, משה, הימן, ידותון, אסף...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the list of authors and explains that ספר תהלים includes psalms from ten elders. The list continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד is credited with writing תהלים, but not all of it is his own. He gathered psalms composed by earlier figures, starting as far back as אדם הראשון.
steps.confusionAlert: "דוד wrote תהלים" does not mean every psalm is his own composition; the ברייתא says he included psalms from ten earlier elders.

phrases.english: David wrote the book of Psalms –
by means of ten elders:
by Adam the first man,
by Melchizedek,
and by Abraham,
and by Moses,
and by Heman,
and by Jeduthun,
and by Asaph,

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּוִד כָּתַב סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים עַל יְדֵי עֲשָׂרָה זְקֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of authors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד compiled תהלים including psalms of ten earlier elders
